title: Peer counseling in social psychiatric centers in the Rhineland – evaluation and findings
summary:
This study examines how peer counseling works in social psychiatric centers (SPCs) and what experiences the participants have had with it. To this end, both the users and the peer counselors and employees of the SPCs are surveyed - partly in interviews and partly using questionnaires.

The background to the study is the funding and  implementation of peer counseling in the SPCs of the Rheinland region by the Rhineland State Council (LVR) since 2020. This form of counseling - in which people with personal experience of mental illness support others affected - has now become established in almost all SPZ. The study aims to find out how well peer counseling works in practice, what challenges there are and how it can be further improved. Of particular interest is how satisfied those involved are, which factors make implementation easier or more difficult and what additional needs there are. The results should help to further develop the service in the long term.

interventions.name: The specific focus of the project is to record and evaluate experiences with peer work in social psychiatric centers (SPZ).
